topic: how applications are read (Slate Reader walkthrough)
speaker_role: former admissions director (Swarthmore) and former Vanderbilt officer, per his own statement
commercial_incentive: Sells a paid application-review service and promotes it early in the video.
key_insights: Files sit in holding bins (awaiting materials, complete) until read; each college defines 'complete' differently, and background rules can auto-move a file once missing pieces arrive.
Readers filter their queue by territory, country, scholarship or other criteria and choose which files to read that day.
The first screen is a dashboard with school data, GPA/rank, round, major, test scores and coded internal tags for demonstrated interest and priority groups like legacy or recruited athlete.
A school-group report shows the current pool from the same high school plus last year's decisions, so a file is read relative to peers with similar GPA.
Rough reading order: dashboard, school group, full application (activities, essays, supplements), then counselor report and letter, school profile, transcript, testing, interview.
Withdrawn applications count in the denominator of admit rate, while a college like Swarthmore excluded files that never became complete.
Rating forms often hold an academic rating plus activity, fit or curiosity-type ratings and terse coded comments; leadership may cap how many files reach final committee.
If waitlisted, he says responding to the offer matters because students who do not respond typically have weaker waitlist chances.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Hoffman: he began in admissions in 2009 with paper files; he says he has read tens of thousands of applications over two decades.
Hoffman (fictitious mock-up): about 50,000 files total, 12,908 in the complete bin, 698 awaiting materials, 243 deferred, 347 withdrawn in mid-January.
Hoffman: college admit rates count withdrawn applications in the denominator.
Hoffman: Florida public school transcripts can run 15 pages, which a territory officer learns to scan quickly.
notable_or_distinctive: A detailed screen-by-screen tour of a mocked-up reading system that makes the sequence and internal coding tangible.
reliability_notes: The software screen is an admitted mock-up with invented data and codes; workflow is described as similar across selective schools but varies, and the video includes a sales pitch.
